2. The petitioner is a banking company incorporated in Bangladesh under the Companies Act, 1913, having its registered office at 71 Dilkusha Commercial Area, Dhaka and having one of its branches at Chapai Nawabganj, Nawabganj. The petitioner being a banking Company is involved in banking business with high reputation and goodwill, including maintaining banking norms, secrecy and confidentiality of the accounts of various clients. The respondent No.1 by its office Memo No. 437/DAB (BAB) dated 7-5-94 addressed to the District and 'Sessions Judge, Nawabganj prayed for issuing direction upon the Manager, Chapai Nawabganj Branch of the petitioner Bank to hand over all MT/TT's statement from July, 1992 to March 1994 sent to different branches of Dhaka and Chittagong for examination and seizure under section 94(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. According to respondent No.1, the said documents were required for preliminary inquiry of the matter of transfer of huge sums through IT and MT by different Banks including petitioner Bank from Nawabganj to Dhaka and Chittagong. The respondent No. 2 issued order allowing the application of the respondent No. 1 for seizure of papers and documents as mentioned in the impugned Annexure and communicated the copy of the order to the petitioner vide Memo No. 619/5 Cr. dated 29-5-94 for information with direction to comply with the same. 

 4. Mr. Ahsanul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has submitted that since no proceeding is pending before any Court relating to the documents maintained with the petitioner Bank, the respondent No. 2, learned District and Sessions Judge, Nawabganj is not empowered under section 94(1)(a) of the Code of Criminal Procedure to direct the petitioner to transmit those documents as prayed by respondent No. 1 for seizure of the same for the purpose of any inquiry. 

 8. Annexure-A is an application made by one Narayan Chandra Sarma, District Anti-Corruption Officer, Nababganj to the learned District and Sessions Judge, Nababganj vide Memo No. 437/DAB (BAB) dated 7-5-94 for permission for seizure of M Ts/T Ts from the period July, 1992 to March, 1994 which were sent to Dhaka and Chittagong Branches, and T Ts and M Ts sent from Nababganj Sonali Bank Branch to Chittagong Sonali Bank Branch favouring account No. CD 624 of one Babul Sheikh. It appears from the said impugned application that the respondent No. 1 made prayer for seizure of the aforementioned documents for the purpose of preliminary inquiry to determine whether any offence under sections 409/477 A of the Penal Code disclosed on such transactions of T T's and M T's. In the said application it is stated that respondent No. 1 was optimistic that after primary inquiry there was likely of disclosure of criminal offence under the above penal sections. From perusal of annexure-A it does not show that any proceeding was pending before any court or to any investigating agency for investigation against any person regarding those documents or there was any allegation or information regarding any particular MT or TT was received, for which the respondent No.1 had reason to have those documents for such inquiry. 

 9. Annexure-C is the order impugned passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Nawabganj allowing the prayer of the respondent No. 1 for seizure of the documents and directing the petitioners bank to produce those banking documents for seizure. Power of the Sessions Judge for direction to produce any banking document for the purpose of investigating any offence by any court or by Officer-in-charge of a Police Station in a proceeding is provided in section 94(1)(a) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Under the said section the learned Sessions Judge can issue summons to any person in whose possession or power such document or thing is believed to be, requiring him to attend or to produce the same at the time and place stated in the summons or orders. This power of the learned Sessions Judge vested by law in relation to the investigation of offences under sections 403/406/408 and 409 and section 421 to 424 and section 465 to 477 A of the Penal Code. It is true that under section 94 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Sessions Judge can summon for production of documents and other thing for the purpose of investigation, inquiry, etc. but power to direct for seizure of documents for such other than in a proceeding is not provided in the Code.  12. We have already found from impugned Annexure A that the respondent No. 1 made application for seizure of the banking documents for the purpose of inquiry to ascertain whether any offence has been disclosed and from impugned annexure-C the order communicated to the petitioner by respondent No. 2, it appears that in exercise of powers under section 94(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Sessions Judge, Nawabganj.Allowed the prayer of respondent No. 1 for seizure of banking documents as referred in annexure-A. 

 17. In the light of our observations made above we are of the view that the order dated 29-5-94 (Annexure-B) passed by Sessions Judge, Nawabganj and memo No. 619/5 Cr. dated 29-5-94 directing examination and seizure of documents from petitioners are made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect.
